headline: Axiom Security Forces Bulldoze Tessera Survey Teams in Lake Grid Dispute
body: Axiom Corporation's private security wing moved against three Tessera survey teams in the contested Lake Grid sector early this morning, destroying equipment and detaining eleven workers before Federal Remnant observers could respond. The disputed zone — a 4.2-kilometer stretch of reclaimed shoreline along what was once Lake Erie's western edge — has been claimed by both corponations since GLMZ's provisional charter left territorial boundaries deliberately vague in 2100. Axiom spokesperson Declan Muroya-Fitch confirmed the operation, calling it 'a lawful defense of licensed development space,' while declining to explain why no warning was issued. Tessera has filed an emergency injunction with the Federal Remnant's Commerce Arbitration Panel, though legal observers note the panel has no enforcement mechanism capable of moving Axiom's security apparatus.
aftermath: The Lake Grid dispute dragged on for seven years before a partition agreement in 2108 split the zone along what became the Ferrogate Transit rail corridor — a boundary still contested in minor skirmishes today.
runner_relevance: The dispute created a booming market for covert survey runners — both corponations paid premium rates for teams that could infiltrate contested ground, plant boundary markers, and extract geological data before rival security could respond. Tessera specifically posted open contracts for the recovery of confiscated survey equipment from Axiom holding facilities, paying up to 8,000 quanta per retrieval. Corporate espionage contracts multiplied as each side sought evidence of the other's legal overreach.
